scope_statement: The ACL role in anterior stability.
source_note: No sources were retrieved. The generation environment had no access to PubMed, Cochrane, any journal or any textbook. The Tier 1 source minimum is NOT met and this draft would not pass Tier 1 in the deployed pipeline. This is the first section on the site written entirely for professionals, and it is unverified.
claims_needing_verification: Restored anterior translation is necessary and insufficient.
A normal reading with an unstable knee is the apportionment argument in clinical form.
Instrumented laxity correlates weakly with patient reported outcome.
Serial measurement is more informative than a single reading.
Progressive laxity without a new injury prompts a slope measurement.
claims_note: Listed above are the substantive claims, taken from the deepest tier's key learning points. Every anatomical statement in the page body requires the same verification against a standard text; these are the ones a reviewer should start with.
content_rule: Decision 006: this page may carry measurements and every one of them is written from standard teaching rather than from a retrieved paper. None has been checked against a source, because the build environment has none. Each figure is registered in pipeline/config/figures/<page_id>.json with the sentence it supports and a verification state, so the checking list is generated from the page rather than compiled by hand. Run tools/figures.py --report --unchecked for the outstanding list.
gaps_or_uncertainties: No measurement appears on this page. Where one would normally sit the page gives the relationship instead, because the value is not one this environment can state with confidence.
Anatomical relations are otherwise described in relative terms, which is adequate for orientation and inadequate for planning that depends on a dimension.
